result.title: Detecting Chain-of-Thought Hijacking in Backdoored Multimodal Large Reasoning Models
result.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning enables multimodal large reasoning models (MLRMs) to solve complex visual problems, but also exposes them to CoT hijacking: an adversary implants a backdoor through poisoned fine-tuning so that a visual trigger induces a hijacking turn, redirecting an otherwise faithful reasoning chain to an attacker-chosen answer. However, since the hijack acts within the reasoning chain, existing multimodal backdoor defenses designed for MLLMs that answer directly struggle to detect it. Moreover, inspecting the chain itself does not reliably expose the hijack, since the hijacking turn can resemble honest self-correction in form. In this paper, we find that honest reasoning tends to revise its answer at high-entropy "aha moments", whereas a hijack can overturn a confident answer through a near-deterministic turn. To quantify this contrast, we formalize this phenomenon as belief inertia, the cumulative next-token entropy of a reasoning span minus the answer-belief revision it induces, with markedly lower values for hijacked spans than for honest reasoning spans. Since hijacking tokens are also image-dependent, we further improve detection by restricting the measure to image-dependent spans, yielding visual belief inertia (VBI). Building on this, we propose InertiaGuard, a training-free, test-time detector that flags a trace when its VBI falls below a threshold calibrated on a small set of clean traces. Across various attacks and benchmarks, InertiaGuard achieves higher detection performance than existing baselines, while generalizing to different model architectures and trigger types.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究多模态大推理模型中的 CoT 劫持后门：提出用「信念惯性」量化推理片段的累积下一 token 熵与其引发的答案信念修正之差，并进一步限定到图像依赖片段得到 visual belief inertia（VBI），据此构建免训练的测试时检测器 InertiaGuard。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及多模态推理链的忠实性诊断，其「答案是否由视觉证据驱动」「哪一段推理真正改变答案」的度量思路，可能与 LVR 中视觉旁路、证据贡献分配及 latent 轨迹监督问题相互参照核查。
